items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: she came in with Jimmy Jones, and so they used our rhythm section... I did a concert this past Sunday and in my group I had Jimmy Jones, piano

ctx.x: Yeah, a little later. And then I went into Birdland with Billy Taylor. We had a group, a quartet. Billy Taylor, Al McKibben, Jo Jones and myself. And we were like the house group, and I would -- oh, if another group came in and didn't have guitars or something I would play with them. And this was the first time I worked with Sarah, because she came in with Jimmy Jones, and so they used our rhythm section, everybody but Billy Taylor. And we just cooked, we had a ball, it was just beautiful.
And I worked there with -- I worked there with Art Tatum, I worked at Birdland with Art Tatum.

items.title: 69537_Jimmy Jones oral history interview
items.q: And he's been an influence musically ever since.

ctx.x: This is December 23rd, and we're continuing the interview with Jimmy Jones, and right after we left off before you said that you wanted to talk about John Collins when we resumed. You said that he had something to do with your not continuing guitar.
Yes. In that the first time I heard John Collins I was with the singing trio, and I was a little

guitar player. We were all influenced by the Mills Brothers in those days. And I heard this man play guitar, and -- oh, now and then I'll pick it up, but after that it stayed in the corner. I said, 'Well, I can't go in that direction, because this man is a master, and he still is a master of his instrument.' Master teacher and everything. He's got the knowledge and -- a complete professional.
